messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool-eu-west-2-3 queue length spike detected
incident-bot: metrics: queue=21,400, avg_wait=18.9s, pct90_wait=29.2s, dropped=42, failed_scale_attempts=6, last_error=PROVIDER_429
incident-bot: autoscaler logs snippet:
```
ERROR 2026-03-15T03:09:12Z scaler.go:412 scaleUp failed: request quota exceeded (429) -> provider throttled
WARN  2026-03-15T03:09:15Z scaler.go:390 retrying (attempt 4)
ERROR 2026-03-15T03:11:03Z poolmgr.go:221 allocate failed: no capacity left in region
```

sophie: I’m paged and looking. switching to pager channel. taking lead for triage. :eyes:
sophie: mike — can you take provider liaison and try bumping quota with cloud contact? raj can you look at the autoscaler controller logs and confirm whether it’s a rate-limit path vs wrong backoff config?
mike: on it. pinging provider support (ticket + 24x7 escalation). I’ll also try a manual pool resize if provider allows.
raj: grabbing controller logs now. initial glance shows frequent 429s from provider and then scaler marks as transient and stops aggressive retries — maybe a safety backoff threshold hit.
sophie: immediate mitigation options: 1) route some traffic to smaller model variant (cpu fallback) 2) apply short-lived stricter per-tenant rate limit to shed non-critical traffic 3) manual pool expand in another region and failover some traffic. which should we attempt first?
elaine: I can prepare a short customer status note if we lock on mitigations. recommend that we aim for routing fallback + rate limiting to reduce queue ASAP.
mike: provider responded: "we're throttling due to burst quota exhaustion in eu-west-2 for your tenant. Estimated recovery 12-18m unless quota increase applied." They offered emergency quota increase but need a support-authorized change. creating auth now.
kevin: ops-bot triggered a dry-run failover policy earlier; I can trigger cross-region failover but will increase latency for EU customers. prefer fallback variant + rate limiting first.
raj: confirming autoscaler config — there’s a conservative cooldown of 10m after 5 failed attempts that is preventing further scale tries. config: `scaleFailuresBeforeCooldown=5`, `cooldown=600s`. That's the safety.
sophie: ok execute plan: (A) apply per-tenant throttle to 20rps for lower-tier tenants (B) switch 30% traffic on read-only routes to cpu-fallback model (C) request provider emergency quota and start manual pool expand in us-west as backup. mike/raj you two coordinate.
mike: starting manual pool expand command now: 
```
# manual create nodes
cloudctl compute create --region eu-west-2 --type gpu-a100 --count 4 --labels pool=eu-west-2-hotfix
```
mike: command returned error: provider rejected create: quota limit reached (429). trying us-west-2 as fallback.
raj: I’ve adjusted autoscaler flags to temporarily relax the backoff so it will attempt scale more aggressively (patch applied to canary controller): `scaleFailuresBeforeCooldown=10, cooldown=120s` — pushing to canary only. monitor closely.
ops-bot: deploy started: autoscaler-canary v1.2.4 -> canary set `eu-west-2-pool-3`
kevin: rolling routing change now: 30% -> cpu-fallback (gradual). monitoring error rates.
elaine: posting customer update draft to #customer-status: "We are seeing elevated inference latency in eu-west-2 due to provider capacity constraints. We are applying fallback routing and rate limits; teams affected may experience degraded throughput for ~30 minutes. We will update in 15 minutes."
sophie: good. mike any luck with provider auth?
mike: provider approved emergency quota for +6 GPU units in eu-west-2 but they are provisioning at their end (ETA ~8 min). entering tracking ticket: SUP-13892.
raj: can see queue starting to drop from 21,400 -> 12,800 since fallback routing applied. pct90 wait down to 12s. still some throttled requests.
incident-bot: monitor: queue=9,600, avg_wait=11.2s, failed_scale_attempts=2
sophie: progress. keep provider in the loop and confirm when new capacity shows up. mike please keep manual expand in us-west on standby.
mike: provider confirmed 4 new nodes added to pool at 03:21 UTC. autoscaler now sees capacity available. triggering controller resync.
raj: controller resync accepted new nodes. starting drain/placement of queued jobs. watch for job failures due to old timeouts.
kevin: started moving backlog to new nodes. queue stabilizing. monitoring for OOM on smaller fallback model routes.
elaine: updated customers: "New capacity is coming online; latency improving. Some customers may still see rate-limited calls. We expect full recovery in up to 20 minutes."
sophie: handing off to mike for next-shift monitoring and postmortem writeup. I’ll be off shift at 03:30 UTC. :white_check_mark:
mike: taking over. notes so far: root cause appears to be sudden burst combined with provider quota exhaustion + conservative autoscaler cooldown which prevented timely retries. mitigations applied: fallback routing, throttling, relaxed cooldown on canary, provider emergency quota, manual cross-region failover standby.
kevin: ops-bot reports queue back down to 800, avg_wait=2.4s, all critical error rates back to baseline.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> degraded -> recovering. timeline: 03:07 alert -> 03:09 triage -> 03:15 fallback routing -> 03:21 provider capacity -> 03:28 queue normalizing.
sophie: thanks team. please add action items to postmortem: 1) reduce autoscaler cooldown but add smarter per-tenant heuristics 2) pre-authorize emergency quota flow with provider for hotpaths 3) add earlier circuit-breaker to automatically route to cpu-fallback at lower queue thresholds 4) add runbook step to notify CS and create customer update faster.
mike: will own vendor quota runbook + SUP-13892 follow-up. raj: will own autoscaler config change and safe rollout. elaine will own customer comms runbook update. sophie — will you draft the postmortem skeleton and tag me/raj for technical details?
sophie: yep, drafting now in ops-postmortems. will include logs and timeline snippets, and we’ll schedule a 30m postmortem review at 10:00 UTC.
kevin: quick ops note: `cloudctl compute list --region eu-west-2 --filter pool=eu-west-2-hotfix` shows new instances id: i-0a1234e5, i-0b2345f6, i-0c3456g7, i-0d4567h8
ops-bot: reminder: create incident channel #inc-5155550000 for the lasting thread and fill incident template.
sophie: created #inc-5155550000 and moved summary. closing this thread once postmortem draft is up. great work everyone. :heart:
